title: Crypto prices edge lower as ETF withdrawals grow; portfolio holds near $71,000
paragraphs: Bitcoin traded near $75,900, down 0.03% over 24 hours, while ether was around $2,239, down 0.18%. Solana slipped 0.31% and XRP lost 0.41%. The major coins were moving modestly lower together, with bitcoin holding up slightly better. All four remained within half a percent of their levels a day earlier. Fund flows provide a more cautious picture of demand than the relatively steady prices alone.

A new weekly analysis from The Block, using SoSoValue data, put US spot bitcoin ETF net outflows at $1.28 billion, taking their year-to-date balance to roughly $914 million of net withdrawals. Ether funds lost another $365 million, their sixth consecutive negative week. Those figures cover completed trading sessions, so they should not be read as fresh weekend selling. They do show that demand through regulated investment products has weakened across both leading assets, leaving less support from that channel.

Binance named Justin Yek, previously a finance executive at Airwallex, to replace departing CFO Kaiser Ng. Co-CEO Yi He said the handover had been planned over the preceding six months and that Ng was leaving for another venture. The transition comes as the exchange deals with its $6.3 billion security breach. Financial leadership and the promised customer reimbursements matter for confidence in a major trading venue, but the announcement does not establish a connection between the departure and the hack.

In developer funding, Umia opened the public auction for Slop Cash, a project that pays for accepted open-source contributions. Umia subsequently said commitments reached the auction maximum in less than 15 minutes. It also reported that demand caused RPC and other infrastructure to lag for some users. The model offers another route to financing software maintenance and agent-assisted development. Auction demand is an early funding signal; sustained use will depend on contributors getting useful work accepted and paid for.

Our on-chain wallets total about $71,047: $11,648 in the active treasury and $59,399 in the Safe. Their combined marked value is down $248, or 0.35%, from the previous comparable snapshot. The Safe now holds 29.52 million ARC directly, up from 26.74 million, and 2.2017 WETH, up from 0.0303. Direct ARC across both wallets is worth about $52,082, or 73% of the portfolio. That concentration remains the largest exposure, despite the increase in directly held WETH.

Beefy positions total $2,223 across pools including WETH/AERO, USDC/cbHYPE and AERO/cbBTC. Aave holds about $7,656 of WETH collateral against $3,146 of USDC debt across both wallets, with health factors of 2.33 in the treasury and 1.86 in the Safe. Fluid is only about $153 net, but carries $1,064 of debt and a 1.03 health factor, leaving little liquidation headroom.
